plainEnglish: Alcohol takes away the three things driving depends on: staying alert, judging situations correctly, and seeing clearly. It does not hit everyone the same way, or even hit the same person the same way twice — your mood, tiredness, other medication and how much you have eaten all change the effect. And there is no trick that speeds up sobering up. Coffee and a cold shower make a drunk person a wide-awake drunk person, nothing more. Only time lowers blood alcohol.
whyItMatters: People get caught out by two beliefs: that they can tell how drunk they are, and that they can sober up quickly if they need to. Both are wrong, and the handbook says so directly. Judgment is one of the first things alcohol damages — which means the part of you deciding whether you are fine to drive is the part already affected.
example: You have three beers over two hours at a friend's house, then drink a large coffee and stand outside in the cold for twenty minutes because you want to drive home. Your blood alcohol has not dropped at all. Worse, because BAC keeps climbing after the last drink, you may be more impaired pulling out of the driveway than you were in the kitchen.

plainEnglish: West Virginia treats drivers under 21 completely differently from adults. For an adult, the question is whether BAC reached 0.08. For someone under 21, there is no threshold to argue about — any measurable alcohol costs you your licence. Separately, simply by driving on West Virginia roads you have already agreed to take a breath test if you are arrested for DUI. Refusing is not a way out: it carries its own revocation of one year up to life, on top of whatever the DUI charge does.
whyItMatters: Two traps live here. The first is thinking 0.08 is a safe line to drive up to — a licence can be revoked below 0.08, and between 0.05 and 0.08 the state can use that reading as evidence of impairment. The second is thinking refusing the test protects you. It does the opposite, and the handbook explains why the law exists: the test protects the driver who has not been drinking by giving a medically accepted measurement.
example: A 19-year-old has one beer at a party and drives home an hour later. An adult with that same BAC might be under every threshold. The 19-year-old is not — any measurable alcohol under 21 means losing the licence, regardless of how fine they feel or how well they drove.

plainEnglish: A prescription from a doctor is not permission to drive impaired. Plenty of ordinary medicines — allergy tablets, cold medicine, painkillers, sleep aids — cause exactly the drowsiness and loss of coordination that make driving dangerous, and mixing them with alcohol is worse than either alone. Being badly short of sleep does the same thing without any substance involved at all.
whyItMatters: People who would never drive after drinking will happily drive after a double dose of cold medicine or a 20-hour day. The handbook puts these in the same chapter as alcohol on purpose: the effect on your reaction time and judgment is comparable, and so is the crash risk.
example: You take an over-the-counter antihistamine for a bad cold before an evening drive. It is legal, it was recommended on the box, and you feel only slightly foggy. That fogginess is slowed reaction time — the same thing you would be criticised for if it came from a beer.

title: Checking Your Vehicle Before It Fails

rules.text: The brake pedal should not go more than halfway to the floor, and should feel like it is hitting something hard.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

rules.text: Test tread with a penny, head first into the deepest groove. If you can see all of Lincoln's head, the tires are too worn to drive on.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

source.sourceQuote: Can you see all of his head?  If yes, your tires

plainEnglish: Most roadside emergencies announce themselves beforehand if anyone is checking. A brake pedal that sinks past halfway, or feels soft instead of firm, is telling you there is air or a leak in the system. Tires that are low on air or tread are the ones that blow out. None of these checks need tools beyond a tire gauge and a penny.
whyItMatters: The handbook puts vehicle checks at the start of the emergency chapter for a reason: the cheapest way to handle a blowout or brake failure is to find the problem in a driveway instead of at 55 mph. Under-inflated tires are specifically named as one of the most common causes of blowouts.
example: Once a month you press the brake pedal before starting off and it feels firm and stops well short of halfway. You check the four tires cold with a gauge against the number on the door jamb sticker, and drop a penny into the tread. Two minutes, and you have ruled out the two failures most likely to put you off the road.

title: When Something Fails at Speed

rules.text: Blowout: hold the wheel tightly, steer straight ahead, ease off the accelerator, and do not brake until the vehicle is under control.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Emergency Situations
source.sourceQuote: Do not brake until the vehicle is under control.

rules.text: Skid: take your foot off the gas and turn the wheel in the direction of the skid. Do not brake unless you are in danger of hitting something.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Emergency Situations
source.sourceQuote: Do not use your brakes unless you are in danger of hitting

rules.text: Fire: smother it with dirt or sand, never water, and move at least 100 feet away if it gets out of control.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Emergency Situations
source.sourceQuote: move at least 100 feet away from the vehicle since the gas tank may explode.

plainEnglish: In almost every sudden failure, the instinct is to hit the brakes — and in most of them, braking first is the wrong move. A blowout has already made the car unstable; braking makes it worse, so you steer straight and let it slow itself before you brake. In a skid, braking locks you into the slide; you lift off the gas and steer where you want to go. The pattern to remember is: get control first, then slow down.
whyItMatters: These are the situations where you get one attempt and no time to think it through. The handbook's instructions are counter-intuitive on purpose, which is exactly why they have to be learned in advance rather than worked out at the time.
example: Your right front tire blows on a 55 mph road. The car pulls hard right. You grip the wheel firmly, steer straight rather than yanking left, and lift off the accelerator without touching the brake. As the car slows and steadies, you brake gently and pull all the way off into a safe area.

title: Your Duties at a Crash

rules.text: Stop immediately, turn off the ignition to prevent fire, and protect the scene to prevent further crashes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Emergency Situations
source.section: If You are Involved In A Crash
source.sourceQuote: Turn off the ignition to prevent the danger of fire.

rules.text: Report a crash involving injury, death, or property damage of $1,000 or more to the nearest law enforcement agency.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Emergency Situations
source.section: If You are Involved In A Crash
source.sourceQuote: you must notify the nearest law enforcement agency.

rules.text: Do not move an injured person unless absolutely necessary; give first aid in the order bleeding, breathing, shock, broken bones.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Emergency Situations
source.sourceQuote: Stay calm and do not move the victim unless there is danger of further injury.

plainEnglish: Your duties run in order: stop, make the scene safe, help the injured, then deal with paperwork. Turning off the ignition is first because fire is the danger that turns a survivable crash into a fatal one. Moving an injured person is the most common well-meant mistake — unless they are in danger where they lie, leave them and send for help. Then exchange name, address, plate number and insurance details, and report it if anyone was hurt or damage reaches $1,000.
whyItMatters: Failing to report a qualifying crash or leaving without exchanging information is not a paperwork slip; it is an offence. And the Good Samaritan law exists so that fear of being sued is not a reason to stand back — someone giving emergency care in good faith, without pay, is not liable for civil damages.
example: You rear-end someone at a light. Nobody seems hurt, but both bumpers are wrecked and a repair will clearly run past $1,000. You stop, switch off the ignition, check on the other driver, exchange name, address, plate number and insurance, and call the nearest law enforcement agency because the damage crosses the reporting threshold.

title: The Habits That Cause Crashes

rules.text: Bad driving habits result from laziness, impatience, inattention, arrogance and aggressiveness.

rules.text: Always turn your head and look behind you before changing lanes, pulling out, or getting out on the traffic side.

source.chapterTitle: Defensive Driving

plainEnglish: The handbook names five specific habits: laziness, impatience, inattention, arrogance and aggressiveness. Laziness is checking only the mirror instead of turning your head, and not bothering to signal. Impatience is rolling a stop sign because nothing is coming and someone is behind you. Inattention is letting your grip and your focus loosen until the car wanders with your mind. Arrogance is treating the car as an extension of your ego.
whyItMatters: None of these are dramatic. They are all small, comfortable shortcuts that feel harmless every time you take them, which is exactly why they turn into habits. The handbook's point is that you have to notice them in yourself and correct them deliberately.
example: You approach a red light intending to turn right. Nothing is coming and the car behind is close. Slowing to 5 mph and rolling through feels safe and considerate. It is still a failure to stop, and it is the habit that will eventually meet a pedestrian stepping off the kerb you did not check for.

rules.text: Dim your headlight beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle, and within 200 feet of a vehicle you are following.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Defensive Driving
source.sourceQuote: means driving too fast to stop safely within the distance clearly lit by your

plainEnglish: Two numbers matter here and they are easy to mix up: 500 feet when you are meeting someone head-on, 200 feet when you are behind them. The bigger distance goes with the bigger risk — blinding an oncoming driver puts two cars in danger. Overdriving your headlights is the subtler idea: if your lights show 200 feet of road but you need 250 feet to stop, you are driving into a space you cannot see.
whyItMatters: At night your stopping distance does not shrink, but your seeing distance does. Most drivers never adjust speed for that. And if oncoming headlights do catch you, the handbook's instruction is specific: slow down, keep right, and look at the right edge of the road rather than into the lights.
example: On an unlit road at 55 mph you meet a car. You dim at about a football field and a half away, and as it passes you fix your eyes on the white line at the right edge rather than the glare, so you keep your lane and your night vision.

title: Rain, Ice, Fog and Standing Water

rules.text: Partial hydroplaning begins at about 35 mph; at 55 mph tires can ride entirely on top of the water with no friction to brake, accelerate or corner.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Defensive Driving
source.sourceQuote: partial hydroplaning occurs on the road at about 35 mph.

rules.text: Never attempt to drive across a flooded roadway. Six inches of water can float a small vehicle; two feet will carry most away.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Defensive Driving
source.sourceQuote: As little as six (6) inches of water can float some smaller vehicles, while two

rules.text: In fog or dense smoke, reduce speed and use low-beam headlights.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Defensive Driving
source.sourceQuote: Use your low-beam headlights.

plainEnglish: Rain is most dangerous when it starts, because oil and dirt lift off the surface into a slippery film before the rain washes it away. As speed rises, the tires stop cutting through water and start riding on it — around 35 mph partially, and by 55 mph potentially not touching the road at all. When that happens you have no braking, no acceleration and no steering. In fog, low beams are correct: high beams reflect off the fog straight back at you.
whyItMatters: Flooded roads deserve their own warning. Nearly half of all flash flood deaths in the United States are motorists trapped in vehicles, and in many cases the road itself has already washed away under the water. Six inches is less than the depth of a kerb.
example: A back road has water running across it after a storm. It looks shallow. You cannot see the surface underneath, you do not know whether the road is still there, and six inches is enough to float the car. You turn around.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Defensive Driving
source.sourceQuote: take a 10-minute rest break at least every two (2) hours.

rules.text: Gain self control over anger, worry or fear before driving.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Defensive Driving
source.sourceQuote: control these emotions and gain self control before driving.

plainEnglish: The handbook's line is blunt: you cannot safely drive 10 feet or 10 miles in an unsafe vehicle. West Virginia backs that with a two-yearly inspection and a windscreen sticker you are not allowed to remove. On the driver's side, the four conditions named are fatigue, alcohol, emotional state, and defective eyesight or hearing — and fatigue gets a specific remedy: stop every two hours for ten minutes, out of the car.
whyItMatters: Emotional state is the one people dismiss. Driving straight after a row, in tears or in a rage, is treated by the handbook as a condition affecting safe operation in the same list as alcohol and fatigue.
example: Three hours into a drive you notice you have stopped checking mirrors and cannot remember the last few miles. That is the point the handbook's two-hour rule was meant to catch. You pull in, get out, walk around for ten minutes.

title: Six Ways Another Vehicle Can Put You in a Crash

rules.text: Assume the vehicle ahead may stop suddenly and without warning; keep a safe following distance.

rules.text: Exceeding the speed limit when passing is illegal.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

source.sourceQuote: Exceeding the speed limit when passing is

plainEnglish: The handbook lists six positions another vehicle can be in before a crash: ahead of you, tailgating you, oncoming, at an angle, passing you, and being passed by you. Each has its own defence. The one people get wrong most often is being passed — treating it as a challenge instead of easing off and letting it happen causes sideswipes and run-off-road crashes.
whyItMatters: Note the handbook's test for passing: if you have to speed to pass, you probably do not need to pass. Exceeding the limit to overtake is illegal, so a pass that only works above the limit is not a legal pass.
example: Someone comes up fast behind you on a two-lane road and pulls out to pass. Rather than holding your speed, you ease off slightly and move right within your lane, which shortens the time they spend on the wrong side of the road.

rules.text: An eight-sided (octagon) sign is always a stop sign, and it means stop completely and give the right-of-way to pedestrians and all cross traffic.

source.sourceQuote: The maximum speed limit in a school zone is 15 m.p.h. when children are present or when specifi ed.

rules.text: A right-side-up triangle with a reflective red border and fluorescent orange centre marks a slow moving vehicle or one that has made an emergency stop.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.section: Single Message Shaped Signs - Triangle (right side up)
source.sourceQuote: A right side up triangular sign with a refl ective red border and fl uorescent orange center identifi es a slow moving vehicle or a vehicle which has made an emergency stop.

rules.text: Shape and colour carry meaning so a sign can be recognised when light, fog, rain, snow or darkness hide the letters.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: The shape and color of signs have meaning.  If fading light, fog, rain, snow, or darkness make it diffi  cult to see the letters, applicants should still know how to recognize a sign and respond accordingly.

plainEnglish: West Virginia reserves a unique outline for each of a handful of critical messages. Octagon is stop, upside-down triangle is yield, pennant is no passing, circle is a railroad warning, pentagon is a school zone, and an upright orange triangle is a slow vehicle. Nothing else uses those shapes.
whyItMatters: On a foggy night or behind a salt-crusted windscreen the lettering may be unreadable long before the outline is. The handbook expects you to identify and obey the sign from its silhouette alone, and permit tests lean heavily on shape-to-meaning recall.
example: You crest a hill at dusk in heavy rain and can only make out a five-sided outline at the roadside. Without reading a word you should already be braking toward 15 m.p.h. and scanning for children, because only a school zone sign is a pentagon.

title: Regulatory Signs Tell You the Law

rules.text: Square and rectangular signs show traffic regulations and guide your speed and direction.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: These signs show traffi  c regulations and guide your speed and direction. These signs tell you about speed limits and other traffi  c laws.

rules.text: Most signs are white with black letters; when the message is very important the sign is red with white letters.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Most signs are white with black letters. When the message is very important, the sign is red with white letters.

rules.text: A red outline with a diagonal bar through it always means NO.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: A red outline with a diagonal bar through it always means “NO.”

rules.text: Speed limit signs show the fastest speed you may drive under optimal weather and road conditions.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: These signs show the fastest speed you may drive under

rules.text: Advisory speed signs at interstate entrance and exit ramps are black on yellow.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: These advisory signs are black on yellow.

plainEnglish: Squares and rectangles carry the rules. White with black letters is the everyday regulatory sign; red with white letters is reserved for the messages that matter most; and any red circle with a slash through it forbids whatever is drawn inside.
whyItMatters: Regulatory signs are enforceable law, not advice. Confusing a black-on-yellow advisory speed with a posted white-and-black limit, or missing a red slash, is how drivers pick up citations they thought they were obeying.
example: A white rectangle reads SPEED LIMIT 55 on a dry clear day, but the ramp ahead carries a black-on-yellow 35. The 55 is the law for the highway under ideal conditions; the 35 is the recommended safe speed for the curve of the ramp, and taking the ramp at 55 is exactly how vehicles roll over.

title: Yellow Diamonds Warn You Early

rules.text: Diamond-shaped warning signs usually appear without explanatory words beneath them, are yellow with black letters, and warn of possible danger ahead.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: These  diamond-shaped signs will usually appear without  explanatory words beneath them.  These signs are yellow with black letters.  They warn of possible danger ahead and may have symbols or written warnings.

rules.text: Pedestrian and school warning signs may be yellow-green with black letters.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Pedestrian and school warning signs may be yellow-green with black letters.

rules.text: Most warning signs are seen without identifying text and instead often have pictures.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: The shapes and colors of signs are a very helpful indicator as to what they are trying to tell you.

plainEnglish: A yellow diamond says something ahead needs your attention: a curve, a crossroad, a merging lane, a hill, a low bridge, a slippery stretch, a crosswalk or a signal. The symbol tells you which. Pedestrian and school warnings may use a brighter yellow-green.
whyItMatters: Warning signs are placed far enough ahead that you can still act. A driver who registers the diamond but does not slow until they see the hazard has already given away the margin the sign was designed to buy.
example: A yellow diamond with a squiggly arrow appears on a rural road you have never driven. There is no advisory plate, so you have no number to obey — but the sign is telling you that the curve cannot be taken at the regular highway speed, so you come off the accelerator before you enter it.

title: Orange Means People Are Working

rules.text: Construction and maintenance signs notify drivers of unusual or potentially dangerous conditions in or near work areas.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Construction and maintenance signs are used to notify drivers of unusual or potentially dangerous conditions in or near work areas.

rules.text: The commonly used work-zone devices are signs, barricades, drums, cones, tubes, flashing arrow panels and flaggers, and orange is their basic colour.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.section: Construction and Maintenance Signs and Devices
source.sourceQuote: The most commonly used traffi  c control devices are signs, barricades, drums, cones, tubes, fl ashing arrow panels, and fl aggers.  Orange is the basic color for these devices.

rules.text: Large flashing or sequencing arrow panels guide drivers into certain lanes and tell them part of the road ahead is closed.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.section: Construction and Maintenance Signs - Flashing Arrow Panels
source.sourceQuote: Large fl ashing or sequencing arrow panels may be used in work zones both day and night to guide drivers into certain traffi  c lanes and to inform them that part of the road or street ahead of them is closed.

rules.text: Flaggers wear orange vests, shirts or jackets and use red-orange flags or stop/slow paddles to direct traffic through work zones.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Flaggers wear orange vests, shirts, or jackets and use red-orange fl ags or stop/slow paddles to direct traffi  c through work zones.

plainEnglish: In a work zone the colour changes from yellow to orange, and the devices change from signs alone to barricades, drums, cones, arrow panels and people. A flagger's paddle carries the same authority as a sign.
whyItMatters: Work zones put people on foot a few feet from live traffic, and the layout can change between one trip and the next. The orange colour is your cue that what you learned about this stretch of road yesterday may not be true today.
example: A flashing arrow panel points left half a mile ahead of a lane closure, and a flagger in an orange vest holds a SLOW paddle. You move left early rather than running the closing lane to its end, and you pass the flagger at a speed that would let you stop for a worker stepping out.

title: Guide Signs Answer Where and How Far

rules.text: Guide signs tell you where you are, what road you are on, and how to get where you want to go.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: These signs tell you WHERE you are, WHAT road you are on, and HOW to get where you want to go.

rules.text: Most guide signs are white on green, motorist services signs are white on blue, and park and recreation signs are white on brown.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Most guide signs are white on green. Motorist services signs are white on blue.   Signs for parks and public recreation areas are white on brown.

rules.text: WV and U.S. route markers are generally black on white.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: WV & U.S. Route Markers - Are generally black on white.

rules.text: Interstate markers are red, white and blue.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Interstate markers -  Are red, white, and blue..

plainEnglish: Green is navigation, blue is services such as fuel and food, brown is parks and recreation. Route markers identify the road itself: black on white for WV and U.S. routes, red white and blue for interstates.
whyItMatters: Reading guide signs early is what keeps you from a last-second lane change across three lanes at an exit — the manoeuvre that causes crashes at interchanges. The colour tells you instantly whether a sign is worth reading now or not at all.
example: Approaching an interchange you see a green sign for EXIT 99 in one mile and a blue sign listing fuel. The green sign decides your lane; the blue one only decides whether you take the exit at all, so you read the green sign first and move right while there is still room.

title: At a Crossing, the Train Always Wins

rules.text: Railroad crossing signs may be round or diamond-shaped yellow signs with black symbols, or black letters on white bars in the shape of an X called a crossbuck.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Railroad crossing signs can be round or diamond shaped, yellow with black symbols, or  black letters on white bars in the shape of an X called a crossbuck.

rules.text: A sign below the crossbuck indicates the number of tracks when there are two or more.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: A sign below the crossbuck indicates the number of tracks when there are two

rules.text: You must yield to all trains, and failure to stop when lights are flashing or a barrier is down will result in a citation.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: You must yield to all trains.  Failure to stop when lights are fl ashing, or a barrier is down, will result in a citation.

rules.text: Where there are two or more tracks, be alert for a second train on the other set of tracks.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: When there are two (2) or more tracks, you must be alert for a second train on the other set of tracks.

rules.text: Do not enter a crossing until the vehicle ahead has moved far enough that you can clear the tracks, or you may be trapped and hit.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: you should not enter a railroad crossing until the vehicle ahead has moved far enough ahead that you can clear the tracks.  Otherwise, you may be trapped on the tracks and hit by another vehicle or by a train.

rules.text: Passing is prohibited within 100 feet of any railroad crossing.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Passing is PROHIBITED in the following places
source.sourceQuote: Within 100 feet of any railroad crossing.

rules.text: Do not change lanes at a railroad crossing.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: DO NOT change lanes in an intersection or at a railroad crossing.

plainEnglish: The crossbuck is the crossing itself; the round yellow sign is the advance warning. Bells, flashers and gates mean a train is coming, and you must yield to every train, every time. Never move onto the tracks unless there is room for your whole vehicle on the far side.
whyItMatters: A train cannot stop for you and needs far more distance than any road vehicle. Most crossing deaths involve a vehicle that was on the tracks with nowhere to go, either because traffic ahead had not cleared or because the driver assumed only one train was coming.
example: Traffic is backed up beyond a crossing at rush hour. The car ahead moves forward but stops with its bumper only two car-lengths past the far rail. You hold behind the crossbuck rather than following it, because if the queue does not move you would be sitting on the rails when the gates come down.

title: Every Signal Indication Has One Meaning

rules.text: On circular green you may enter the intersection and go straight, right or left unless other devices prohibit the movement.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Drivers facing this signal may enter the intersection and go straight through, turn right, or left, unless, other traffi  c control devices (signs or pavement markings) prohibit certain movements.

rules.text: A driver facing circular green who wishes to turn left must yield to oncoming vehicles.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: A driver who is facing a circular green indication and wishes to turn left must yield to oncoming vehicles.

rules.text: A green arrow lets you enter the intersection to make the movement shown by the arrow.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: A green arrow may be shown alone or with other indications.  Drivers facing the signal may enter the intersection to make the movement shown by the arrow.

rules.text: A green arrow in a left-turn signal usually means opposing traffic is stopped.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: When the green arrow is shown in a left-turn signal, it usually means that opposing traffi  c is stopped.

rules.text: Steady yellow means the green is ending; only drive through it if the vehicle clearance is within the intersection.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: This means that the green light is ending and will change to red.  You should only drive through a yellow light if the vehicle clearance is within the intersection.

rules.text: A yellow arrow means the green arrow is ending and will change to red.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Yellow Arrow / LEFT TURN - This means that the green arrow is ending and will change to red.

rules.text: Traffic facing steady circular red must stop and remain stopped until another indication allows it to proceed.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Traffi  c facing a steady circular red signal must stop unless making a movement permitted by a green arrow.  The driver must remain stopped until allowed to proceed by another indication.

rules.text: Right on red is allowed at two-way streets and left on red from one-way to one-way, after yielding to all traffic and pedestrians and if no sign prohibits it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: A driver may turn right on red at the intersection of two-way streets, or may turn left on red from a one-way street to another one-way street.  These turns may be made after yielding to all other traffi  c and pedestrians, and if no signs are posted to prohibit them.

rules.text: A steady red arrow requires a complete stop before the intersection, stop line or crosswalk, and you remain stopped while it is red.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Come to a complete stop before reaching the intersection, stop line or cross walk for the direction indicated by the arrow.  Remain stopped as long as the signal is red.

plainEnglish: Green is permission, not priority — you still yield when turning left. A green arrow is protection, because opposing traffic is normally stopped. Yellow means the phase is ending, and red means stop until something changes, with turn on red as the only exception.
whyItMatters: Intersections are where the most conflicting paths cross, and signal questions appear on every permit test. The difference between a permissive green ball and a protected green arrow is the difference between yielding and going, and getting it wrong causes head-on left-turn crashes.
example: You are waiting to turn left on a circular green with two cars coming the other way. The green ball does not give you the intersection — it only lets you into it — so you wait for a gap. If the signal changes to a green arrow, opposing traffic is stopped and the turn is yours.

title: Flashing Signals and Signals for People

rules.text: Flashers are installed at certain intersections to supplement or replace STOP signs.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: At certain intersections, fl ashers are installed to supplement or replace STOP signs.

rules.text: Drivers facing a circular flashing yellow may proceed through the intersection with caution.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Drivers facing a circular fl ashing yellow light may proceed through the intersection

rules.text: A circular flashing red is the same as a stop sign, so drivers must come to a complete stop and yield.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: A circular fl ashing red is the same as a stop sign; that is, drivers must come to

rules.text: Signals that are not needed or are out of order may be placed in flashing operation, and then mean the same as intersection flashers.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: When traffi  c control signals are not needed or are out of order, they may be placed in fl ashing operations. When this happens, they are the same as intersection fl ashers.

rules.text: Lane use control signals control traffic where the direction of a street or lane changes during the day.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Special signals are used to control traffi  c when the direction of a street or certain lane changes during the day.  These signals indicate how the specifi c lanes may be used.

rules.text: Crosswalk signals are traffic signals for pedestrians, and pedestrians are to obey them.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Crosswalk signals are traffi  c signals for pedestrians.  If these signals are in place, pedestrians are to obey them.

rules.text: A hand symbol or DON'T WALK means pedestrians are not to cross.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Hand Symbol or DON'T WALK- when these appear pedestrians are not to cross the crosswalk.

rules.text: A walking man or WALK means pedestrians are safe to cross inside the crosswalk lines.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Walking Man or WALK - when these appear  pedestrians are safe to cross the street inside the crosswalk lines.

rules.text: A blind person using a guide dog, service animal, white cane or walking stick has the right-of-way whether or not they are in a crosswalk.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: A blind person who is on foot and using a guide dog or other service animal, or is carrying a white cane or walking stick, has the right-of-way on a highway, street, or road regardless of whether they are in a crosswalk or not.

plainEnglish: Flashing red is a stop sign; flashing yellow is a caution. A dead or unneeded signal put into flashing operation means exactly the same thing. Pedestrian signals govern people on foot, but a blind pedestrian has the right-of-way regardless.
whyItMatters: A signal that has failed is one of the most dangerous intersections on the road, because drivers on each approach may be reading different indications. Knowing that flashing red equals a stop sign is what keeps a power cut from becoming a broadside collision.
example: A storm has knocked the signals at a four-way junction into flashing operation: red toward you, yellow across. You stop completely and yield as if at a stop sign, and you do not assume the cross traffic will stop — their flashing yellow lets them roll through with caution.

title: The Lines Are Instructions Too

rules.text: Pavement markings are used like highway signs to warn, regulate and inform traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Pavement markings are used like highway signs to warn, regulate, and inform traffic.

rules.text: White lines separate traffic lanes moving in the same direction.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: WHITE lines separate traffic lanes moving in the SAME direction.

rules.text: Yellow lines separate traffic lanes moving in opposite directions.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: YELLOW lines separate traffic lanes moving in the OPPOSITE direction.

rules.text: A broken yellow line on your side means you may pass when it is safe.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Broken yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.  If this marking is on your side of the road, you may pass when it is safe.

rules.text: A solid yellow line on your side means you MUST NOT PASS.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: If a solid yellow line is on your side of the road, you MUST NOT PASS.

rules.text: Broken white lines separate same-direction lanes; drive within them and never straddle them except when changing lanes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: On roadways which have more than one (1) lane moving in one direction, traffic lanes are separated by broken white lines.

rules.text: Solid white lines mark the pavement edge, and where they separate same-direction lanes, DO NOT CHANGE LANES.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Solid white lines mark the edge of the pavement.  At night or in bad weather, they help you stay on the road.  When solid white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, DO NOT CHANGE LANES.

rules.text: White diamonds mark a lane designated for car pools, bicycles or buses.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: White diamond shapes painted in the roadway to inform drivers the lane is designated for car pools, bicycles, or buses.

rules.text: Centre left-turn lanes are reserved for left turns from either direction and are not to be used as through or passing lanes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Center Left-Turn Lanes - These lanes are reserved for left turns from either direction and are not to be used as through or passing lanes.

rules.text: Reversible lanes are marked on both sides by a double broken yellow line, the only case where a driver may drive any distance to the left of a yellow line.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Lanes which reverse are marked on both sides by a double yellow broken line.  This is the only case where a driver may drive for any distance to the left of a yellow line.

rules.text: Wide white stop lines mark where you must stop; with no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Stop Lines - Wide white lines, painted across traffic lanes, mark where you must stop your vehicle at intersections.

plainEnglish: Colour tells you who is on the other side: white means traffic going your way, yellow means traffic coming at you. Broken means you may cross it when it is safe; solid means you may not.
whyItMatters: Markings are the only traffic control device present continuously along the whole road, and at night they are often all you can see. They also decide the legality of a pass on a two-lane road, which is the manoeuvre with the highest head-on crash risk.
example: On a two-lane road you pull out to pass a slow truck while the yellow line on your side is broken. Halfway along, the line on your side becomes solid. You must be back in your lane by then, because the solid yellow is telling you sight distance has run out for oncoming traffic.

title: Speed Limits Are a Ceiling, Not a Target

rules.text: Exceeding the speed limit endangers the lives of others as well as your own; observe limits and adjust to conditions.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: When you exceed the speed limit, you endanger the lives of others as well as your own. Observe speed limits and adjust your speed to the driving conditions.

rules.text: The higher the speed, the less time you have to spot hazards and judge the speed of other vehicles.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: The higher the speed, the less time you have to spot hazards, judge the speed of other vehicles, and act to avoid personal mistakes and those of other drivers.

rules.text: West Virginia law prohibits driving at a speed greater than reasonable and prudent for existing conditions.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: West Virginia law prohibits driving at a speed that is greater than reasonable and prudent for existing conditions.

rules.text: Interstate maximum speed is 70 mph unless otherwise posted.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Interstate - Maximum Speed 70mph unless otherwise posted

rules.text: Open county highway is 55 mph unless otherwise posted.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Open County Highway - 55mph - unless otherwise posted

rules.text: Business or residential areas are 25 mph.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Business or Residential Areas - 25mph

rules.text: A school zone is 15 mph while children are present along the roadway.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: School Zone (while children are present along the roadway) - 15mph

rules.text: A school zone extends 125 feet along the street or highway from the school grounds.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: A school zone is all school property, including school grounds, and/or any street or highway abutting the school grounds and extending 125 feet along the street or highway from the school grounds.

rules.text: Slow down for intersections, curves, hilltops, narrow roads, and conditions that limit visibility or stopping distance.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: To ensure your safety, and the safety of others, you should slow down when you are faced with these driving situations:

rules.text: Authorized emergency vehicles on emergency duty with signal equipment operating may exceed posted limits if other road users are not endangered.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Authorized emergency vehicles may exceed the posted speed limits when on emergency duty with emergency signal equipment operating, as long as other road users are not endangered.

rules.text: Driving slower than normal traffic means keeping as close as possible to the right edge of the road.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: When you drive at less than the normal speed of traffi  c, you should drive as close as possible to the right edge of the road.

rules.text: If you must drive slower than the designated speed, pull off at the first safe turnout to let faster traffic pass.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If you must drive slower than the designated speed, pull off  at the fi rst safe turnout to let faster moving traffi  c pass.

plainEnglish: Learn the four designated limits — 70, 55, 25, 15 — but understand that the posted number is the maximum for ideal conditions. Rain, fog, traffic or a narrow road can make a legal speed an illegal one.
whyItMatters: Speed decides how much time you have to react and how hard the impact is if you do not. It is also the one rule where a driver can be cited while technically under the posted limit, because the basic speed law measures against conditions, not signs.
example: You are on an open county highway posted at 55 when fog drops visibility to a few hundred feet. Holding 55 is a violation of the basic speed law even though the sign says 55, because you can no longer stop within the distance you can see.

title: Turning Well Starts Long Before the Corner

rules.text: Turn signals tell other drivers you intend to turn or change lanes, since they expect you to continue straight.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Other drivers expect you to continue traveling in the same direction.  By using your turn signals, you let them know that you intend to turn or change lanes.

rules.text: Signal at least 100 feet before you plan to turn, every time.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Get into the habit of signaling every time you make a change.  Signal at least 100 feet before you plan to turn.

rules.text: Signal at least 100 feet before turning.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Signal at least 100 feet before turning.

rules.text: Switch off your signals after the turn; a signal left on creates confusion.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Switch off  your turn signals after completing the turn.  Driving with turn signals on without intending to turn can create confusion.

rules.text: If you plan to turn beyond an intersection, do not signal so soon that drivers think you are turning at the intersection.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If you plan to turn beyond an intersection, do not confuse other drivers by signaling too soon.

rules.text: Before entering the turning lane, signal, check the mirrors, and check the blind spot over the proper shoulder.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Before entering the turning lane, signal, look in the mirrors, and check the blind spot by glancing over the proper shoulder.

rules.text: Slow down before making turns, and do not brake while turning.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Slow down before making turns.  Do not brake while turning.

rules.text: Always finish turning in the proper lane.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Always fi nish turning in the proper lane.

rules.text: When turning left, watch for approaching traffic in the opposite lane.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: When turning left, watch for approaching traffi  c in the opposite lane.

rules.text: When waiting to turn left, do not turn the wheels to the left, or a bump from behind could push you into oncoming traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: When waiting to turn left, do not turn the wheels to the left.  Otherwise, a bump from behind could push your vehicle into oncoming traffi  c.

rules.text: Where no sign prohibits it, traffic facing red may turn right after a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If an intersection has no signs prohibiting a turn on red, traffi  c facing a red signal may, after coming to a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and traffi  c, make a right turn.

rules.text: Improper turns cause many crashes, and pedestrians and bicyclists are often the victims.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Improper turns cause many traffi  c crashes.  Pedestrians and bicyclists are often victims of improper turns by vehicle operators.

plainEnglish: A good turn is planned: signal 100 feet out, check mirrors and blind spot, lose the speed before the corner rather than in it, and come out in the correct lane. Waiting to turn left, keep the wheels pointed straight ahead.
whyItMatters: Turning puts you across someone else's path, which is why improper turns injure so many pedestrians and cyclists. The wheels-straight rule is the one most drivers have never heard, and it is what stops a rear-end shunt from becoming a head-on collision.
example: You are stopped in an intersection waiting for a gap to turn left, wheels already angled toward the gap. A distracted driver hits you from behind and your car is pushed straight into oncoming traffic. Had your wheels been straight, you would have been shoved forward into the empty intersection instead.

title: Turning Around and Backing Up

rules.text: It is against the law to turn around near a curve, or near the crest of a hill where you cannot be seen by a vehicle approaching within 500 feet in either direction, or where signs prohibit turning.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: it is against the law to turn your vehicle around near a curve, near the crest of a hill where you cannot be seen by another vehicle approaching within 500 feet in either direction, or where signs  prohibit turning.

rules.text: Before backing, check completely around the vehicle for people and obstacles, and keep looking to the rear while backing rather than depending on the mirror.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Before backing, check completely around your vehicle for people and/or other obstacles.  You should look to the front, sides and rear and continue to look to the rear while backing. Do not depend on your mirror.

rules.text: Backing in a traffic lane is not advisable except when backing into a parallel parking space, and you must never back across traffic lanes or through an intersection.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: It is not advisable to back up while in a traffi  c lane, except for backing into a parallel parking space.  Never back across other traffi  c lanes or through an intersection.

rules.text: When backing out of an angle parking space, do not back across the centre line.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Angle Parking (§17C-13-4, W. Va. State Code)
source.sourceQuote: Remember, do not back across the center line.

rules.text: Be extra watchful when backing in or out of a driveway for children who may have run behind the vehicle.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: As a driver, be extra careful in residential areas, school zones and at times and places where children are likely to be around.

plainEnglish: Turn around only where approaching drivers can see you from at least 500 feet. When backing, look with your eyes and your body, not just the mirror, and never reverse across other lanes or through an intersection.
whyItMatters: Reversing is the manoeuvre with the worst visibility and the highest proportion of child pedestrian injuries, because a small child behind a vehicle is invisible in every mirror. A turnaround at a blind crest gives an oncoming driver no time at all.
example: You miss your turn on a two-lane road and the nearest wide spot is just past the top of a rise. Turning there is illegal because a car coming the other way would only see you once it crested — so you carry on to a driveway with clear sight lines in both directions.

title: Park Legally and Leave It Safe

rules.text: Vehicles must always be parked in the same direction as the movement of traffic on that side of the street.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Vehicles must always be parked in the same direction as the movement of traffi  c on that side of the street.

rules.text: Avoid double parking; it is illegal and discourteous.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Avoid double parking. It is illegal and discourteous.

rules.text: Whenever you park and leave the vehicle, turn off the engine and set the parking (emergency) brake.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Whenever you park and leave your vehicle, you must turn off  the engine and set the parking (emergency) brake.

rules.text: Stopping, standing or parking is not allowed on a sidewalk, in front of a driveway, within an intersection, on a crosswalk, or in front of a wheelchair ramp or curb cut.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Prohibited Parking (§17C-13-3, W. Va. State Code)
source.sourceQuote: Stopping, standing or parking is not allowed (except to avoid a confl ict with other traffi  c or to obey a law, police offi  cer or a traffi  c signal) in the following locations:

rules.text: No parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Prohibited Parking (§17C-13-3, W. Va. State Code)
source.sourceQuote: Within 15 feet of a fi re hydrant

rules.text: No parking within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Prohibited Parking (§17C-13-3, W. Va. State Code)
source.sourceQuote: Within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection

rules.text: No parking within 30 feet of any stop sign or traffic control signal.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Prohibited Parking (§17C-13-3, W. Va. State Code)
source.sourceQuote: Within 30 feet of any stop sign or traffi  c control signal

rules.text: No parking within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Prohibited Parking (§17C-13-3, W. Va. State Code)
source.sourceQuote: Within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing

rules.text: No parking within 20 feet of any mailbox served by a carrier using a motor vehicle for daily deliveries.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Prohibited Parking (§17C-13-3, W. Va. State Code)
source.sourceQuote: Within 20 feet of any mailbox served by a carrier using a motor vehicle for daily deliveries

rules.text: No parking upon any bridge or other elevated structure or in a highway tunnel.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Prohibited Parking (§17C-13-3, W. Va. State Code)
source.sourceQuote: Upon any bridge or other elevated structure or in a highway tunnel

rules.text: A curb in a no-parking zone may be painted yellow.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Prohibited Parking (§17C-13-3, W. Va. State Code)
source.sourceQuote: Any place where official signs prohibit parking.  A curb in a no-parking zone may be painted in yellow

rules.text: Parking on a grade means turning the front wheels to the curb side of the highway so the vehicle will not roll, and setting the brake.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If you park or stop on a grade, turn the front wheels to the curb side of the highway so the vehicle will not roll.  Be sure to set the emergency or parking brake.

rules.text: Parallel parked wheels should be within 18 inches of the curb, facing the direction of traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Parallel Parking (§17C-13-4, W. Va. State Code)
source.sourceQuote: When parallel parking on the left side of the road, wheels should be within 18 inches of the left curb.  Park in the direction of the traffic.

rules.text: It is illegal to park in a designated mobility impaired space without a placard or license plate.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: It is illegal to park a vehicle that does not display a mobility impaired parking placard or license plate in a designated area.

plainEnglish: Park with traffic, close to the curb, engine off and brake set. Memorise the four distances — 15 feet from a hydrant, 20 from a crosswalk at an intersection, 30 from a stop sign or signal, 50 from the nearest rail — because they are asked directly.
whyItMatters: Badly parked vehicles hide pedestrians from drivers and drivers from each other, and block the exact places emergency crews need: hydrants, crossings and intersection sight lines. The hill rule is what stops an unattended car rolling into traffic.
example: You find the only gap on a downhill street just past a stop sign. Measure it: if your bumper sits closer than 30 feet to the sign you are blocking the view of every driver approaching it, so you move on. Where you do park, you turn the wheels toward the curb and set the brake before you get out.

title: Buy Yourself Seconds, Not Feet

rules.text: Following too closely causes most rear-end collisions, and the space ahead is the space easiest to control.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Following too closely causes most rear-end collisions.  The space ahead of your vehicle is the space easiest to control.  This space cushion is called the following distance.

rules.text: The best way to assure proper following distance is the three-to-four second rule.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: The best way to assure proper following distance is to use the three-to-four second rule.

rules.text: Count one thousand one, one thousand two, one thousand three from when the vehicle ahead passes a fixed object; reaching it first means you are too close.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: To use the three-to-four second rule, choose a fixed object on the road ahead (such as a signpost, tree, overpass, or bridge abutment).  When the vehicle ahead passes that object, begin to count “one thousand one, one thousand two, one thousand three.”

rules.text: If it is dark or raining, the distance should be at least four seconds.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If it is dark or raining, the distance should be at least four seconds.

rules.text: If there is ice or snow, stay at least six seconds behind the vehicle in front.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If there is ice or snow, stay at least six seconds behind the vehicle in front.

rules.text: Keep a minimum three-to-four second following distance behind a motorcycle, and increase it at night and in bad weather.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Motorcyclists are entitled to and will need the entire lane to maneuver around possible hazards and traffic situations.  It is wise to keep a safe minimum three -to-four second following distance.

plainEnglish: Measure your gap in seconds, not car lengths, because seconds scale automatically with speed. Three to four seconds is the baseline, four in the dark or rain, six on ice or snow.
whyItMatters: The distance you need grows faster than your speed does, so a gap that is safe at 30 mph is dangerously short at 70. Counting seconds is the only method that stays correct at every speed without any arithmetic.
example: You are behind a pickup at 60 mph and pick out a bridge abutment ahead. The pickup passes it and you count one thousand one, one thousand two — and you are already level with it.
